description:
MAIN-PARA re-entry at app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:82-92 into PROCESS-ENTER-KEY's ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :117-151, arm four of five. In source order: SET ERR-FLG-OFF TO TRUE at :73; MOVE SPACES TO WS-MESSAGE and to ERRMSGO OF COUSR1AO at :75-76; IF EIBCALEN = 0 is false at :78 because the payload carries all 160 bytes of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA; MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN) TO CARDDEMO-COMMAREA at :82; IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is false at :83 because CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives as 1, so the first-entry paint at :84-87 is skipped and PERFORM RECEIVE-USRADD-SCREEN runs at :89; EVALUATE EIBAID at :90 matches WHEN DFHENTER at :91 and performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :92. Control leaves through EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) at :107-110, which is why termination is RETURN_TRANSID and not XCTL: the only transfer in this program is RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN's XCTL at :175-178, reachable solely from the EIBCALEN guard at :79-80 and from WHEN DFHPF3 at :93-95, and neither is on this path.

An EVALUATE is ordered and the first matching WHEN wins, so this case is about arm four only if the three before it are demonstrably false. FNAMEI, LNAMEI and USERIDI all arrive non-blank, so :118, :124 and :130 are false; PASSWDI arrives as eight spaces, so :136 is the first arm to match and neither the fifth arm at :142 nor the WHEN OTHER at :148 is ever consulted. Arm four then executes MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG at :137, moves its message at :138-139, positions the cursor with MOVE -1 TO PASSWDL OF COUSR1AI at :140 and performs SEND-USRADD-SCREEN at :141. That an operator can submit a blank password without noticing is a property of the map rather than of the program: PASSWD is declared ATTRB=(DRK,FSET,UNPROT) at app/bms/COUSR01.bms:126, so the field is non-display and an empty one looks exactly like a filled one.

Nothing reaches USRSEC. Arm four raised WS-ERR-FLG, so IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON at :153 is false, the five MOVEs that build SEC-USER-DATA at :154-158 do not run, and PERFORM WRITE-USER-SEC-FILE at :159 is never reached - the EXEC CICS WRITE at :240-248 and all three RESP arms at :250-274 are unreached here. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion that nothing was written anywhere; expectedFinalState pins all ten rows so that no observed row is left unaccounted for; and expectedDatasets adds the dataset-level statement that USRSEC holds exactly ten rows at an 80-byte layout on the FINAL_STATE channel, which is the only way to assert that no eleventh row appeared, since a row expectation can only address a row that exists. A WRITES-channel expectation is deliberately not declared: this path never opens the dataset for output, and claiming it there would assert a behaviour the program does not have.

The five data items keep exactly what the RECEIVE delivered. INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :287-294 is performed from two places only - CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN at :281, which is the DFHPF4 arm, and the DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm of the write at :252 - and this path reaches neither, so FNAMEO, LNAMEO, USERIDO, PASSWDO and USRTYPEO are the received values at the symbolic map's widths of 20, 20, 8, 8 and 1. COUSR1AO REDEFINES COUSR1AI at app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:91, so the xxxI item the RECEIVE filled and the xxxO item the SEND transmits occupy one span of storage; nothing on this path overwrites those five spans, so the echo is the received image and PASSWDO is the same eight spaces that selected the arm.

The message narrows twice and both widths are pinned. The literal at :138 is 'Password can NOT be empty...', which is 28 characters. It is a program-local literal and not a CSMSG01Y message: CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY, the only message this program takes from app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy, belongs to the WHEN OTHER arm at :101 and is not this text. The MOVE at :138-139 targets WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at :38, and an alphanumeric MOVE left-justifies and space-pads, giving 28 + 52 = 80 - the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel. SEND-USRADD-SCREEN then performs MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO OF COUSR1AO at :188, where ERRMSGO is PIC X(78) at app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:164, so the same rule truncates on the right and drops the last two of those spaces, giving 28 + 50 = 78 - the SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 channel. The chain is 28 -> 80 -> 78, and the two channels are stated separately on purpose: comparing one against the other would let the truncation pass unnoticed.

SEND-USRADD-SCREEN performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO first, at :186, so the six header items are repainted from working storage on every send and never echoed from the request. TITLE01O and TITLE02O are CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy at their declared PIC X(40), and TITLE02O is the CardDemo literal rather than the '  Credit Card Demo Application (CCDA)   ' one, which is commented out in that copybook. TRNNAMEO is WS-TRANID 'CU01' from :37 and PGMNAMEO is WS-PGMNAME 'COUSR01C' from :36. CURDATEO and CURTIMEO come from MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :216, reassembled as mm/dd/yy at :224-228 and as hh:mm:ss at :230-233 - which is why the clock has to be pinned for a header assertion to be possible at all. The instant is 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the source's own version footer at :298, and the code page is named as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default.

The cursor is metadata, not payload. COBOL positions it by moving -1 into the symbolic map's length item, so PASSWDL - a COMP PIC S9(4) at app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:73 - is the cursor, and it is declared as cursorField rather than as a member of the send's field map, as are the xxxF and xxxA items. No highlight is asserted because none exists: COPY DFHATTR at :57 is commented out, COUSR01C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY, and the single attribute assignment anywhere in the program is MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :254 on the confirmation. ERRMSGC therefore carries the default colour, DFHDFCOL, and there is no '*' marker and no per-field DFHRED on this arm or on any other. The bright red ERRMSG a terminal would show is the map's own doing - ERRMSG DFHMDF ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) COLOR=RED LENGTH=78 at app/bms/COUSR01.bms:151-154 - and not something the program writes.

USRSEC is seeded with the ten in-stream rows of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 verbatim, at their real width of 57 characters. There is no usrsec fixture under app/data/ASCII - the nine that exist are for other datasets - which is why the rows are inline rather than a fixture reference. app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy declares SEC-USR-ID X(08) + SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) + SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) + SEC-USR-PWD X(08) + SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) + SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) = 80, so the span the JCL omits is exactly the trailing FILLER. That pad has one owner: it is declared once here as USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 and applied at seed time, never at comparison time, so a width disagreement in a failure is always a real difference and never a missing declaration. SEC-USR-PWD stays plaintext in the eighty-byte images because that is what the program writes and what COSGN00C compares; hashing it would need Spring Security, which is out of scope, and would change behaviour, which is forbidden.

Provenance: every expected value here is statically derived, and none of it was captured from a running COBOL program. Executing the legacy programs is impossible in this environment for eight independently verified reasons - among them no z/OS runtime, an available compiler that reports 'indexed file handler : disabled' so the programs using ORGANIZATION INDEXED cannot even build, no Language Environment CEE* services, no CICS emulator, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from the repository altogether. This baseline is therefore a substitution of provenance and only of provenance: twenty cases, field-for-field diffing and a required diff count of zero all stand. The values above were obtained by reading app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:73-110, :117-160, :184-196 and :214-233 statement by statement and cross-checking app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record's byte layout, app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY with app/bms/COUSR01.bms for the screen's field shapes and attributes, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy for the title literals, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the header's date and time items, app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy for the message this arm does not use, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the 160-byte communication area, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl for the seed data. It is stated here rather than in a commit message because a statically derived expectation can encode a misreading of the COBOL where a captured one cannot, and whoever debugs a failure needs to know which side to doubt.
